newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN PLAYERS OFFERED REWARD TO COME SECOND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN PLAYERS OFFERED REWARD TO COME SECOND.

text.p: For the first time in their history, Italian champions AC Milan are offering their players a reward for coming second.

Newly appointed coach Arrigo Sacchi admitted last week that his side, suffering one of their worst seasons in recent years, could not retain the Serie A title they have won four times in the past five seasons.
They are currently eight points adrift of leaders Juventus and have also been knocked out of both the European and domestic cup competitions.
But, under new rules to be introduced next year, second place in the league will be good enough to take a team into the lucrative European Cup Champions' League.
Consequently, Milan are offering their players 100 million lire ($65,000) each if the team clinches that second place, a club official said on Sunday.
They will get 500 million lire if they defy their coach and finish first.
